html:
John A. Macdonald was the first prime minister of Canada, from 1867 to 1873 and from 1878 until his death in 1891. Born in Glasgow, he grew up in Kingston, Ontario, where he became a lawyer.

He was the main architect of Confederation and pushed the country west, building the Canadian Pacific Railway, though the Pacific Scandal over railway funds forced him out in 1873. His National Policy put tariffs on imports to protect Canadian industry.

His government had Louis Riel hanged in 1885, withheld food from starving Plains peoples to force them onto reserves, and set up the residential schools. Once honoured on banknotes and in statues, he is now a disputed figure, and several of his statues have been removed.
